policy: Grammar-profile evidence is a curriculum prior, not learner-state authority.
A broad lesson-page level range does not prove that every sub-form belongs at the lower bound.
Bundled LINGUA grammar concepts may span multiple source rows/levels; no level is auto-promoted.
LINGUA_A0 is internal Pre-A1 scaffolding, not an official CEFR-J or Council of Europe lexical/grammar level.
No grammar concept is production-approved by this audit alone.

evidence: British Council Present simple: 'to be' is in A1-A2 grammar
records.rationale: Both sources place ordinary present be in beginner/A1-oriented material. LINGUA may surface a narrowly scoped identity/location/state subset earlier only as an explicitly internal Pre-A1 bootstrap.

evidence: British Council comparative adjectives are taught in the A1-A2 grammar section / beginner reference
records.rationale: Comparative morphology spans A1-A2. LINGUA_A2 is a reasonable consolidated-core band if the concept scope stays limited to common -er/more + than comparisons and excludes advanced comparison constructions.

evidence: CEFR-J CL.if ADVERBIAL CLAUSE: if A2.1 (generic/indirect evidence)
British Council Conditionals: zero, first and second is a B1-B2 grammar lesson and directly teaches first conditional
records.rationale: The CEFR-J row set does not expose a clean first-conditional row, but the British Council independently places explicit first-conditional instruction in B1-B2 material. Keep B1 as a proposal pending human scope review.

evidence: British Council Past continuous and past simple is in the A1-A2 grammar section
records.rationale: Past-simple forms emerge across late A1 and A2. LINGUA_A2 is defensible for a consolidated affirmative/negative/question core, while individual high-frequency affirmative forms may be encountered earlier.

evidence: British Council Present simple is in the A1-A2 grammar section
records.rationale: Core present-simple use is strongly A1-oriented, but some form combinations appear later in CEFR-J. Keep the concept narrow: common affirmative, negative and question patterns for routines/general truths.

evidence: British Council Defining relative clauses is a B1-B2 grammar lesson
records.rationale: Individual relative markers occur earlier, while productive clause-level use spans wider levels. B1 is suitable only for a tightly defined productive bundle (basic defining clauses with who/that/which); advanced omission, non-defining clauses and complex attachment stay outside scope.

evidence: CEFR-J PP.I_am A1.1 and related personal-pronoun + be patterns cluster around A1
British Council Personal pronouns marks subject/object pronouns as beginner grammar
records.rationale: Subject pronouns are foundational beginner material. LINGUA can introduce I/you/he/she/we/they in its internal Pre-A1 bootstrap without claiming an official CEFR-J A0 assignment.

evidence: No direct there-is/there-are row found in the inspected CEFR-J Grammar Profile
British Council Using 'there is' and 'there are' is explicitly A1-A2
records.rationale: A direct independent teaching source supports A1-A2 placement even though the CEFR-J grammar CSV lacks a clean matching row. Keep LINGUA_A1 as proposal pending human sign-off.
